idea: Early-thirties West Yorkshire medic who stays quiet: an under-the-breath clinical call, then a stunned rising question that turns to anger only on the last word. It is the most restrained option, for if the shouting reads as cartoonish.
script:
Sats dropping... he's peri-arrest!

Why have we... stopped?!
tone: An English man in his early thirties with a warm West Yorkshire accent, ordinary and working class, a tired night-shift paramedic. He says the first line low and quick, almost to himself, tense and breathy, eyes on the monitor. The second line starts quiet and stunned, then rises into anger by the end, hoarse and disbelieving. Understated, close and intimate, like a serious British hospital drama, a single dry voice.
